extracted.intended_audience: AAAI-26 authors and reviewers (conference paper submitters/evaluators)
extracted.subtask_description: A conference-required checklist authors must complete to document transparency and reproducibility of AAAI submissions; reviewers use it as one factor in evaluation. Covers general paper reporting, dataset reporting, and experimental reporting items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of mathematical setting/algorithm/model
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear description of the mathematical setting, algorithm, and/or model
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist requires that submissions include an explicit, clear description of the formal problem setup and the methods used (mathematical formulation, algorithms, or models) so reviewers can understand and reproduce the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of contribution and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear specification of the contribution and what is novel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly state what the paper's contributions are and what aspects are novel relative to prior work; this helps reviewers judge originality and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations of the approach are clearly stated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose limitations of their approach; being explicit about failure modes, scope, or assumptions improves transparency and reviewer assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs for theoretical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical claims have proofs (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making theoretical assertions, provide proofs or clear pointers to proofs; if proofs are omitted, justify why or provide sketch/appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset availability or access instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset is publicly available or detailed access instructions provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a dataset, either provide a public URL or explicit, detailed instructions for how other researchers can obtain the data (including access requests, credentials, or steps if not fully public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation to the source of the dataset
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the original dataset source (papers, dataset release pages, or creators) so provenance is clear and credit is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of data filtering/preprocessing/augmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of any data filtering, preprocessing, or augmentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact details of preprocessing steps (e.g., normalization, tokenization, augmentation procedures) and any filtering applied to raw data so experiments can be replicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset splits described
rubrics_metrics.description: Splits clearly described
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how training/validation/test splits were created (random seed, stratification, cross-validation protocol, held-out sets) including counts or proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics about the dataset (size, label distribution, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report dataset-level statistics such as number of examples, class/label distributions, feature dimensions, and other summary statistics that affect reproducibility and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Code is publicly available or will be made available upon publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should release code (or commit to releasing upon publication) to enable exact reproduction; if code cannot be released, provide a clear justification and alternative reproduction materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperparameter selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperparameter selection process is described
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how hyperparameters were chosen (e.g., search ranges, tuning method, validation protocol). This includes whether choices were tuned on validation or test data and any selection heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of all hyperparameters
rubrics_metrics.description: All hyperparameters used are specified
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List all hyperparameter values used in reported experiments (learning rates, batch sizes, regularization, architecture details, seeds) rather than only high-level settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of training runs reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of training runs reported
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how many independent runs were executed for each experiment (e.g., number of random seeds) so variability can be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation across runs reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Variation across runs reported (error bars, confidence intervals)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report measures of variability (standard deviation, confidence intervals, error bars) across runs to show reliability and robustness of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardware specifications (GPU/CPU type, memory)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details about computational environment (GPU/CPU models, number of devices, memory) that can materially affect runtime and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate training time and computational cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximate training time and computational cost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give approximate wall-clock training time and indicative compute costs for experiments (per run and total) so others can judge feasibility and resource requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical significance tests used to compare to baselines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If comparisons are made, describe the statistical tests used and report p-values or other significance measures to justify claims of improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of baseline choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of baselines is justified
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why selected baselines are appropriate and include strong/representative comparisons; avoid cherry-picking weak baselines without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responses required for each item
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must provide responses for each item, and "no" responses require justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For every checklist item authors should answer (yes/no/n/a) and supply justifications for negative answers. A 'no' or 'n/a' is not automatic grounds for rejection if adequately justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use of checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be asked to use the checklist as one factor in their evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist is an input to reviewer judgments rather than an absolute gate; reviewers consider authors' checklist responses alongside the paper's content when evaluating transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis for empirical papers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper includes experiments, a "no" answer regarding reproducibility will not be perceived well by reviewers—particularly for hyperparameter specification, number of runs and variability, and code availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical papers are held to higher expectations on reproducibility-related items; missing information in key experimental areas (hyperparameters, runs/variability, code) negatively influences reviewer perception and assessment.
